counter_evidence:
(1) The claim says folding in any order gives an IDENTICAL INDEX. It does not, because FTS5 returns tied results in rowid order, and rowids follow ingest order. Test: node:sqlite 3.53.4 on Node v24.22.1, script ksc2/fts_tie.cjs in the scratchpad. Two entries with the same text ("android build broke", the ex7/ex8 shape) and the same bm25 (-5.2234e-06) were inserted in two orders. Order ex7,ex8,other returned [ex7 rowid 1, ex8 rowid 2]. Order ex8,other,ex7 returned [ex8 rowid 1, ex7 rowid 3]. The ranking order in sec3-5 §4.1 step 3 is exact hit, then coverage, then BM25, with no unique final key. The design itself records an ex7/ex8 coverage tie (§4.1 step 4). With margin 0 there is no lead, and the one candidate shown is then decided by ingest order. That order is readdir order on a rebuild: sorted on NTFS (checked, top and leaf dirs sorted), and not guaranteed sorted on a Linux VPS. So a rebuilt index, or a second host, can show a different candidate card from the source for the same query.
(2) The index is not a function of the event set alone. It is a function of the events AND the CLI build. sec3-5 §3.3 says a recipe change re-derives keys, §4.1 says it re-derives every handle, and §5.1 lists recipe, runner and scrub version changes as invalidation triggers (4)-(6). Yet §3.1 keys the index file only by schema version (index/ks-i<N>.sqlite). Architect D's worktree_story says "tools/ks may differ between worktrees", and agents run the CLI from their own worktree (architect A access: node tools/kb/kb.mjs). So two worktrees with the same schema but different recipes write one shared index, and the result depends on which CLI derived it last. A restore with a newer CLI re-derives different handles.
(3) based_on_version is an INTEGER (architect A DDL: "version, content_sha, based_on_version: INTEGER, TEXT, INTEGER"). An integer base does not identify a version across hosts. Toy fold of A's stated rule, ksc2/fold.cjs: 2000 shuffles gave exactly 1 result, so the (lamport, event_id) tie-break is total and ordering is not the problem. But host A's state before sync (v3, provisional, content A-edit-2) differs from the merged state. Two reasonable readings of "stale base -> conflict" also give different current content: A-edit-2 laid on top of B-edit, or B-edit. KS-A2's line that this "gives the same conflict detection" as D's parent DAG holds only for detecting that a conflict exists, not for knowing which base the author saw.
(4) Pure-add merging assumes every committed file's bytes hash to its name. D's write path (step 7) commits with "git add events lookups", and its two_host_story syncs with "commit, then git pull --no-rebase". Neither checks hashes or excludes *.tmp-<pid> files. git refuses to merge over an untracked file whatever its content: the string "untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge" is in ucrt64/libexec/git-core/git.exe, and the git-merge.html PRE-MERGE CHECKS section says pull/merge "will stop without doing anything". So an interrupted pull leaves incoming files untracked, and possibly truncated, because checkout writes them in place. The next sync then either refuses, or commits a truncated copy under the hash name, which gives an add/add conflict under events/. The never-do list forbids deleting journal files, which blocks the obvious recovery. This is reasoned from git's behaviour, not tested, because I could not run git writes.
(5) Windows long paths. In the scratchpad, git hash-object failed with "Filename too long" on a 293-character event path, and succeeded with -c core.longpaths=true. core.longpaths is not set in the system config; it is set only in this worktree's config.worktree. The design's default home gives a 135-character path, which is safe. A deeper custom home is not.
(6) Durability. git-config.html says the platform default is "core.fsync=committed,-loose-object ... risks losing recent work in the event of an unclean system shutdown".
The pure-add claim itself is not refuted for distinct, well-formed files. The commit-latency claim is supported by proxy, not by a real git measurement (see trace).
what_would_settle_it:
Two tests in KS-1, which needs git writes in a scratch store the owner allows:
1. Time real `git add` + `git commit` of 300 and 1,000 event files on top of a 20,000-event store, with core.fsync including loose objects and core.fsyncMethod=batch, with Defender or the installed scanner on and off.
2. Interrupt a `git pull` during checkout, then run ks sync again, to see whether the commit-then-pull sequence refuses or commits a hash-mismatched file.
design_consequence:
1. Retrieval tie-break: end every ranked list (prefilter hits, coverage, BM25, the shown lead and candidate) with entry_id ASC. On rebuild, ingest in (lamport, event_id) order, not readdir order.
2. Fold-equality test: the KS-1 test must compare a digest over entry_state, the derived handle rows, and the top-k output for a fixed query set (including an ex7/ex8 tie) across shuffled ingest orders and across Windows and Linux. A digest of entry_state alone is not enough.
3. Version keying: record recipe_version, runner_version and scrub_ruleset_sha in index meta, and either name the index file by them or refuse to open (and rebuild) on any mismatch in either direction. Worktrees run different tools/ks against one shared index.
4. Revision base: name the base of an authored revision by content (the base version's content_sha or its event id), not by an integer, so a merged fold knows which version the author saw.
5. Commit path: stage only events/**/<h>.json files whose sha256 equals h, never `git add events`. Add a .gitignore for *.tmp-*. Quarantine mismatches outside events/. In ks sync, handle a stale .git/index.lock and the "untracked files would be overwritten" refusal by verify-then-commit (identical bytes make a clean add/add), never by deletion. Add that recovery to the never-do list's allowed actions.
6. Store repo config, set by the CLI: core.longpaths=true (or ks doctor refuses a home path that would push event paths past about 250 characters); core.fsync covering loose objects with core.fsyncMethod=batch (documented as safe on NTFS); explicit --no-rebase; an explicit branch name for the bare repo, because the system gitconfig sets init.defaultbranch=master.
